text:
I even hear how

the mountains laugh

up and down their blue slopes

and down in the water

the fish weep

and all the water

is their tears.

I hear the water

the nights I consume drinking

and the sadness grows so large

that I hear it in my watch

it becomes knobs on the dresser,

it becomes paper on the floor,

it becomes shoehorn,

laundry ticket,

it becomes cigarette smoke

climbing a temple of dark vines...

Little matters,

little love

or little life

is not so bad.

What counts

is watching the walls

I was born for that.

I was born to steal roses from the avenues of death.

translation.title: Culmination of Pain
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the expanding sadness, ordinary objects, and final rose-theft from death.
